task_name: The conversation's values, its ports and its failures

rubric.result: The objective promises five things and each one is in the diff: the conversation (`conversation-id.ts` with the uuid guard and `.text`, `coordinating-conversation.ts` with `{id, repository, root}`), the phase prompt (`phase-prompt.ts`, `PhasePrompt.brainstorming({story, comment, repository, root})` with `.text`), the attention (`session-attention.ts`, `AttentionStatus` frozen plus `working()`/`waiting(question)`), the three ports (`conversations.ts`, `session-hooks.ts`, `conversation-records.ts`) and each failure with the refusal it owes (`exceptions.ts` gains two families with two leaves each, and `start-plan-route.ts` gains the four `PlanCollapse` rows `conversation-not-started`, `conversation-not-recorded`, `session-hooks-not-written`, `session-hooks-not-understood`). The prompt composed in `PhasePrompt.brainstorming` is English, which is what the amended decision 12 of the plan and `CLAUDE.md` require, and what the previous attempt was vetoed for.

The **TDD:** line names a test that already belongs to this repo: `every_way_the_plan_can_collapse_has_a_refusal_declared_so_adding_one_cannot_reach_the_client_as_a_crash`, red the moment the four leaves exist and green once `PlanCollapse` declares their rows. I read it at `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/plan-refusal.test.ts:75-79`: it compares `PlanCollapse.declaredFailures().sort()` against every exported `PlanFailure` descendant that is not a registered family root, which is exactly the assertion the plan describes. The diff's only test change is registering the two new roots in `FAMILIES` (line 57) — the brief asks for it in as many words ('That guard's `FAMILIES` list registers the two new roots, the way every family before them was added') and it does not exempt the four leaves, which still have to appear in `declaredFailures()` and do. Same assertion, same input, same expected value.

Symbol by symbol against the brief's blocks: `Conversations` declares `mint(): ConversationId`, `isResumable(conversation): boolean`, `start({conversation, promptPath}): LiveSession`, `resume(conversation): LiveSession`; `SessionHooks.install(root: CheckoutRoot): Promise<void>`; `ConversationRecords.prepare({conversation, prompt}): Promise<string>` and `recall(): Promise<CoordinatingConversation | null>`; `CoordinatingConversation {id, repository: RepositoryName, root: CheckoutRoot}`; `ConversationId` guards the uuid shape and carries `.text`; `PhasePrompt.brainstorming({story, comment, repository, root})` with `.text`; `SessionAttention` with `working()` carrying `question === null` and `waiting(question: string | null)`; `AttentionStatus = Object.freeze({ WORKING: 'working', WAITING: 'waiting' } as const)` verbatim. The four exception leaves, the two family roots and the four kebab-case codes are literal. One divergence: the brief's block writes `readonly status: string` while the diff writes `readonly status: AttentionStatusValue` and exports that derived type. That is the contract narrowed to the closed vocabulary `conventions/defects.md` demands ('A value that classifies something is a member of a closed vocabulary, not a string compared by hand'), and the brief's own contract line that declares `AttentionStatus` is what the diff honours; I record it here rather than as a finding.

Rows the diff bears on: D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) — the seven new modules are `.ts` with `.ts` extensions on their imports, implemented. D-16 (cmux leaves the backend) — no new module names cmux. D-25/D-26 (the phase prompt travels as a path, hydrated from the ticket) — `PhasePrompt` is a value carrying `.text`, and the path is `ConversationRecords.prepare`'s return, with no prompt text in any argument; the hydration from `story.key/summary/description` and from `comment.text` is what D-26 spells. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented) — nothing of the plugin is transcribed; `BRAINSTORMING_SKILL` is the skill's invocation name and appears once in the tree. D-1, D-13, D-18, D-21, D-22 and the entrance button's literal have no subject in this diff and are left alone. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: `conversation-id.ts` is the `user-story-key.ts` idiom line for line (`static #SHAPE`, `EXAMPLE`, `readonly text`, `isWellFormed`, `toString`, `Object.freeze(this)`); `coordinating-conversation.ts` matches `session-program.ts`/`user-story.ts` (named-argument constructor, freeze, and no re-check of what the argument types already guarantee, which `conventions/domain.md` asks for); the three ports match `backend/src/domain/ports/live-sessions.ts` and `user-stories.ts` (`throw new Error(\`${this.constructor.name} must implement …\`)`, the previous attempt's `?.` on non-nullable parameters is gone); the four `PlanCollapse` rows are the `#collapsed('kebab-case')` idiom of their neighbours and nothing else of `start-plan-route.ts` moved. Rules: `conventions/style.md` — no comment or docstring anywhere in the new modules, every identifier and the composed prompt in English ('Code is written in English' plus `CLAUDE.md`, which refuses the declared-debt exemption for language), and every function hangs off a type (`PhasePrompt.#idea` is a private static method, not a loose helper). `conventions/architecture.md` — domain imports only domain, the new files sit in `domain/value-objects` and `domain/ports` where the folder is the discriminator, and the exceptions go into the one `exceptions.ts` catalogue this repo declares together on purpose. `conventions/decisions.md` — nothing here is a second wording of a rule already written elsewhere; `'working'`/`'waiting'` exist nowhere else in `backend/src`. `conventions/boundaries.md` — the four causes reach four distinct codes, declared explicitly beside their detail and never derived from a class name; the quieting rule ('Text from another system gets its active syntax quieted before it enters a document of a third one') has no subject here, since the prompt is a file read by the session and not an issue body where `#7` autolinks. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — `AttentionStatus` is frozen and `status` is typed by the vocabulary, not by `string`; the only dispatch touched, `PlanCollapse`'s `Projection`, raises for an unmapped member instead of falling into a catch-all. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: the ports answer `ConversationId`, `LiveSession`, `Promise<string>` (the path the contract asks for) and `Promise<CoordinatingConversation|null>`; `#idea` returns a `string[]` consumed inside its own class, and the object literals are parameters, not returns. (3) two fields that have to agree — `SessionAttention` holds `status` and `question`, and the private constructor with the two named scenarios makes 'working with a question' unrepresentable; the absence travels as `null` in the type, not as an empty-string sentinel. (4) an error named for where it happens — the four leaves are named for what happened (`NotStarted`, `NotRecorded`, `NotWritten`, `NotUnderstood`), none for a module. Two tensions I declare instead of reporting, because the diff could not resolve them: `ConversationFailure`'s two causes are both 'the command failed', where `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` ('Every family under `PlanFailure` names its two causes') and `conventions/domain.md` ask for the unreadable-answer cause — the brief's contract names those two leaves and the task's own verification pins `grep -c 'extends ConversationFailure' -eq 2`, and the plan already records it as decision 13 with its provenance; and `SessionHooks` carries a tool's noun, which `conventions/domain.md` warns about, but the name is dictated by the contract block and by the endpoint the slice's end state names.

The diff has one test file, `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/plan-refusal.test.ts`, and it carries no `-` line: the only change is `+    'ConversationFailure', 'SessionHooksFailure',` inside `FAMILIES`. No assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten, so this item has no subject. For the record, that addition does not weaken the guard: the four new leaves are not in `FAMILIES`, so `startingAPlan` still demands a declared row for each of them, and the brief asks for the registration by name.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code and by nothing in a test's scaffolding: the vocabulary lives in `backend/src/domain/value-objects/` and `backend/src/domain/ports/`, the families in `backend/src/domain/exceptions.ts`, and the guard turns green because `PlanCollapse.#BY_FAILURE` really gained four rows in `backend/src/infrastructure/start-plan-route.ts:320-323` — revert those four production lines and `declaredFailures()` no longer matches the exported leaves, so the test falls. Nothing is hard-coded in the test to stand in for a production line.

Inside the declared files, every line serves a sentence of the task: the seven new modules are the vocabulary the objective names, `exceptions.ts` gains exactly the two families and four leaves the contract spells and nothing else, `start-plan-route.ts` gains four import names and four projection rows and nothing else of that module moves, and the test file gains only the `FAMILIES` registration. `### Out of scope` is respected: nothing under `plugin/skills/brainstorming/`, and `POST /start-plan` keeps its behaviour, its use case and its adapters — the four `PlanCollapse` rows are the one exception the amended scope section names. The plan hunk is the one place to weigh: it is a mid-run amendment that adds `start-plan-route.ts` and `plan-refusal.test.ts` to this task's `**Files:**` (it removes no route from it), rewrites task 2's contract, TDD and tests to say that the rows land in this commit — justified, because the guard makes a leaf without its row impossible to ship separately — and leaves the task's four verification commands identical but for trimmed comments, so no control was disarmed. The rest of the hunk (task 7 losing `start-plan-route.ts` now that the rows moved here, the split of task 11 into 11 and 12 with the renumbering it forces, and decisions 12, 13 and 14) is plan repair beyond task 2's own sentences, declared with its provenance in the plan's decision list and touching no production code; I record it rather than report it.

The diff adds no test. Its only change to a test file is one line registering two family names in the `FAMILIES` constant of a guard that already existed, which is the subject of `manipulacion-tests`, not of this item. With no new test to measure as an instrument, there is nothing here to check for determinism, isolation or real behaviour, and the `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` skill was therefore not needed: it governs the finer half of a finding about a new test, and no such finding exists.
